class.name: SplatterDecals3D
class.brief_description: Leaves decals where flying drops would land, for example blood behind a hit.
class.description: When [method splatter] is called, [member count] rays are cast from this node inside a cone of [member spread] degrees around [member direction], up to [member max_distance]. Each ray that hits a physics body in [member collision_mask] puts a [Decal] with [member texture] on that surface, turned to its normal and rolled at random. The decal appears after the time a drop flying at [member drop_speed] needs to get there, stays for [member lifetime] seconds and fades out over [member fade_time]. GPU particles cannot report where they land, so the rays stand in for them: give this node the same direction and spread as the emitter of the drops. At most 64 splatter decals exist at once; the oldest make room for new ones. As a child of a [ParticleEffect3D] it fires automatically at its start time (see [method ParticleEffect3D.set_emitter_delay]) and takes the tint and scale the effect plays with. It only works in the running game, because the rays need the level's physics.

method.name: splatter
method.description: Casts the rays and places the decals now. Inside a [ParticleEffect3D] the decals are added next to that effect, otherwise next to this node.

members.member: The physics layers that can be splattered.
Number of rays, and so the largest number of decals of one splatter.
Middle of the cone the drops fly in, in this node's space.
Speed of the drops in meters per second; a decal appears when a drop would arrive. [code]0[/code] shows all of them at once.
Seconds a decal takes to fade out at the end of its [member lifetime].
Seconds a decal stays before it fades out.
How far a drop flies; surfaces farther away stay clean.
Color the decals are multiplied by.
Optional normal map of the decals.
Smallest and largest size of a decal in meters; each one gets a random size between them.
Half angle of the cone in degrees.
Texture of the decals. Nothing is placed without one.
